question: do conserved RT-core anchors map across broad RT-class diversity at all
population: all sufficiently represented RT classes in the frozen instrument's scope
stratification: RT class; identity-distance bin; completeness; source database
estimands: E01 mapping reproducibility; E05 class transfer; E04 ordering
outputs: per-class mapping-success rate with call states; failure modes named
what_would_falsify_the_shared_frame: a class in which mapping fails for most full-length members while succeeding in its neighbours
precedence: runs FIRST; everything else is conditional on it

question: which anchors are broadly shared and which are lineage-restricted
outputs: anchor occupancy matrix, class by anchor, with inspectability retained

question: where do RT classes differ in architecture
estimands: E11 inter-anchor spacing; region length; normalized position
outputs: spacing and length distributions by class; insertion/expansion candidates

question: is an apparently missing anchor architecture, truncation, or transfer failure
population: sequences with at least one NOT_DETECTED anchor
stratification: completeness class; contig-edge state; identity distance; flanking-anchor success
outputs: per-sequence resolution into UNINSPECTABLE_PARTIAL, local non-detection with intact flanks, or global transfer failure
precedence: after A3; gates every use of the word absent

question: RT0 in group II introns versus retrons
population: full-length sequences only, with a non-LTR comparison class
outputs: nothing until the substrate and comparison class exist
precedence: BLOCKED - E09 is UNESTABLISHED and RT0 stays OUT_OF_FRAME

question: do retron RTs map onto the general frame at the same rate as other classes
stratification: retron type; identity distance; activity stratum where supported
outputs: retron mapping-success rate compared against the per-class distribution from A1
what_would_falsify_the_shared_frame: if retrons map at a rate far below the distribution of other classes, the general frame has failed FOR RETRONS specifically
precedence: runs after A1 and is the decision point for B-extension

question: which anchors differ in retrons relative to other classes
outputs: retron anchor occupancy and spacing against the cross-class background

question: retron-specific insertions and unusual architectures
outputs: retron insertion length distributions; outlier architectures retained and flagged
denominator: retron sequences with both flanking anchors

question: relationship to later structural and ncRNA analyses
outputs: coordinate handoff tables only; no inference in Stage 2

question: the general frame is derived ONCE, on the broad panel, and is frozen before either view runs
retrons are an ANALYSIS stratum, not a derivation stratum, unless B1 demonstrates systematic failure
what_would_falsify_the_shared_frame: a retron-specific extension is proposed only on B1 evidence, never pre-emptively

question: if a retron-specific extension is built, it is an EXTENSION of the shared coordinate system, reporting where it diverges, not a second independent frame
precedence: binding - two unrelated frames would make cross-class comparison impossible, which is the whole point of View A

question: every occupancy statement carries its call state, its inspectability and its denominator; a class-level rate is never computed over sequences that could not physically show the anchor
